# How the proof works: Kourovka 21.44

**Agent-generated exposition; not refereed.** This informal account was generated by **Nilradical v0** after human acceptance of the linked proof snapshot. It has not undergone human review or refereeing and may simplify details. The exact mathematical claims are the linked Lean statements and their proofs; human acceptance of that snapshot does not imply human review of this exposition. The [human decision](../nilradical-v0-acceptance/README.md) and [technical verification](../nilradical-v0-verification/README.md) are separate records.

Sean Eberhard's question concerns the inverse limit $W$ of iterated permutational wreath products of $A_5$, always in its natural action on five points. The $n$-th finite level acts on $5^n$ points. The answer supplies one fixed pair of elements whose ordinary generated subgroup $G$ is dense in $W$ and has subexponential word growth. The [public statement](https://github.com/alunik/kourovka-lean/blob/5a6b2c18e326b7b0281f00b64cade629acbfe1f5/Kourovka/Problems/P21_44/Statement.lean#L20) fixes this ambient group and topology; only the finitely generated dense subgroup is existentially quantified.

In right-action notation, with branches numbered 1 through 5, the pair is given recursively by

$$
\begin{aligned}
a &= (1,1,1,a,1)(1\ 2\ 3), \\
b &= (b,1,1,1,1)(3\ 4\ 5).
\end{aligned}
$$

Each tuple gives the actions on the five subtrees below the root; the final cycle gives the root permutation. Thus each generator repeats itself in just one subtree and acts trivially inside the other four. Finite recursion defines compatible elements at every depth, giving actual infinite tree automorphisms $a$ and $b$. Lean uses zero-based `Fin 5` and inverse reindexing for multiplication, so its stored root cycles are the inverses of $(0\ 1\ 2)$ and $(2\ 3\ 4)$, with active sections at 3 and 0. [The wreath definitions](https://github.com/alunik/kourovka-lean/blob/5a6b2c18e326b7b0281f00b64cade629acbfe1f5/Kourovka/Problems/P21_44/Proof/Wreath.lean#L13) fix this convention before the calculations.

The ambient `AutTree` is the full subgroup of compatible sequences in the product of the finite levels. Each level has its discrete topology; the inverse limit inherits the product topology. There is no additional support restriction on its elements. A tree automorphism is determined by its root permutation and five actual sections, meaning its induced actions on those subtrees. The construction proves this faithful decomposition and proves that a subgroup surjecting onto every finite level is dense: any open neighborhood prescribes only finitely much finite-level information.

Density is an algebraic induction. Suppose $P$ is perfect and generated by $u$ and $v$, with $u^3 = v^3 = 1$. The two directed lifts of $u$ and $v$ generate $P^5 \rtimes A_5$. Their root permutations generate $A_5$, so the remaining problem is to obtain the whole base $P^5$. Explicit fifth powers of products of the lifts give base elements whose first coordinates include $uv$ and $uv^{-1}$. Using the cube relation recovers $u$ and $v$ in that coordinate, and root transitivity yields surjectivity onto every coordinate.

Surjectivity onto individual coordinates is not enough by itself to recover a direct product. The proof strengthens it to every pair of coordinates. For one selected pair, conjugation by a directed lift acts as conjugation by $u$ in one coordinate while leaving the other alone. The resulting quotient argument forces the possible common quotient to be abelian; perfectness makes it trivial. Two-transitivity of $A_5$ transports full pair projection to every pair. A general lemma for finite powers of perfect groups then gives the entire base. This is the content of [`Wreath.generates`](https://github.com/alunik/kourovka-lean/blob/5a6b2c18e326b7b0281f00b64cade629acbfe1f5/Kourovka/Problems/P21_44/Proof/WreathGeneration.lean#L237).

Every finite wreath level is perfect, and the recursively defined generators satisfy the cube relations. Consequently `levels_generate` applies the preceding theorem inductively. [`generated_pair_surjective` and `dense_generated_pair`](https://github.com/alunik/kourovka-lean/blob/5a6b2c18e326b7b0281f00b64cade629acbfe1f5/Kourovka/Problems/P21_44/Proof/Density.lean#L28) then concern the same fixed pair at every level. This compatibility is essential: choosing unrelated generating pairs in the finite quotients would not establish the advertised dense two-generated subgroup.

The growth proof measures ordinary balls for $S = \{1,a,a^{-1},b,b^{-1}\}$. Since 1 is included, $S^n$ consists of products of at most $n$ letters. `wordGeometry` uses these actual finite sets, and its volume $\gamma(n)$ is their cardinality. Every ball contains the identity. The target conclusion is precisely $\log\gamma(n)/n \to 0$ as $n$ tends to infinity. The accepted result is qualitative; it supplies no additional explicit asymptotic growth rate.

Because $a^3 = b^3 = 1$, every word can be normalized, without increasing length, to alternate between the $a$-family and the $b$-family, with a positive or negative sign on each letter. Define $V(w)$ to count sign changes between letters two positions apart. These are consecutive occurrences of the same generator family in an alternating word. Many such changes create cancellations when the word is routed into its five sections.

The finite starting point is [`five_letter_shortening`](https://github.com/alunik/kourovka-lean/blob/5a6b2c18e326b7b0281f00b64cade629acbfe1f5/Kourovka/Problems/P21_44/Proof/Shortening.lean#L11): sixteen signed five-letter patterns each have section representatives of total length at most four. A greedy selection takes disjoint occurrences, so no saved letter is counted twice. The variation estimate bounds $V(w)$ by ten times the number of selected patterns plus six. Combining these facts gives the convenient uniform inequality

$$
\sum_i \ell(g_i) + \frac{V(w)}{10} \le |w| + 1,
$$

where $g_i$ are the five sections of the element represented by $w$ and $\ell$ is ordinary word length in $G$. The additive one is retained throughout the subsequent count.

This passage from routed words to actual lengths is a central Lean bridge. `treeSection_mem_generated` proves that each actual section belongs to $G$, and `generatedSection` places it in the subgroup type. The theorem [`generated_section_shortening`](https://github.com/alunik/kourovka-lean/blob/5a6b2c18e326b7b0281f00b64cade629acbfe1f5/Kourovka/Problems/P21_44/Solution.lean#L18) bounds its least word length by the length of a proved representative. Finally `root_sections_injective` ensures that root-and-section data distinguish group elements. Those facts make the combinatorial estimate applicable to ordinary word growth.

Fix $0 < \delta < 1/2$. Words of length at most $n$ with $V(w) \le \delta n$ admit a compact encoding: their length, the first generator family, the first two signs, and the positions of the sign changes. The three initial bits give a factor eight; the length gives $n+1$ choices. A Bernoulli-weight estimate for small subsets bounds their total number by $8(n+1)\exp(nH(\delta))$, where

$$
H(\delta) = -\delta\log\delta - (1-\delta)\log(1-\delta)
$$

is binary entropy. [`card_smallWords_le`](https://github.com/alunik/kourovka-lean/blob/5a6b2c18e326b7b0281f00b64cade629acbfe1f5/Kourovka/Problems/P21_44/Proof/WordEncoding.lean#L198) proves this encoding bound.

Every remaining ball element has an alternating representative with more than $\delta n$ variations, hence total section length at most $(1-\delta/10)n+1$. Suppose $\gamma(k) \le C\exp(sk)$ for all $k$. Counting the 60 possible roots, possible five-tuples of section lengths, and corresponding section balls bounds this part by

$$
60(n+2)^5 C^5 \exp\!\left(s\left((1-\delta/10)n+1\right)\right).
$$

Injectivity justifies the upper bound without requiring arbitrary section tuples to be realizable. [`wordGrowth_recurrence`](https://github.com/alunik/kourovka-lean/blob/5a6b2c18e326b7b0281f00b64cade629acbfe1f5/Kourovka/Problems/P21_44/Proof/Counting.lean#L24) adds the two contributions.

The analytic finish considers the infimum of positive rates $s$ admitting such a uniform exponential bound. These rates exist from the elementary bound for finitely generated word balls. If their infimum were positive, choose $\delta$ small enough that $H(\delta)$ lies below it, then choose an available $s$ sufficiently close to the infimum that $(1-\delta/10)s$ also lies below it. The recurrence would give a strictly smaller available rate. Polynomial factors are absorbed in the strict gap, and finitely many initial radii are covered by changing $C$. This contradiction forces infimum zero; positivity of ball volumes then gives the logarithmic limit. No growth-rate limit is assumed in advance.

The sign-change counting method has prior context in **Jérémie Brieussel's** [work on directed automorphism groups](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00209-008-0417-3), also presented in Proposition 3.6.6 of his thesis. Nilradical v0's contribution here is the degree-five construction and its integrated proof, including the density and actual-section bridges. Ordinary word geometry and general logarithmic-growth foundations come from **Konstantin Slutsky and contributors'** `recurrent-sections-lean`, under Apache-2.0; [the provenance record](https://github.com/alunik/kourovka-lean/blob/5a6b2c18e326b7b0281f00b64cade629acbfe1f5/Kourovka/Problems/P21_44/Proof/THIRD_PARTY.md) identifies the upstream commit and retained modules.

Computation is confined to explicit finite facts. A Python breadth-first search produces 60 root words, of maximum length eight; Lean's `rootWords_cover` checks their coverage by ordinary `decide`, and `roots_generate` derives generation. The sixteen shortening cases also use kernel-checked `decide`. The external search supplies data, not a trusted conclusion. For reading, start with [`subexponential_growth` and `notebookStatement`](https://github.com/alunik/kourovka-lean/blob/5a6b2c18e326b7b0281f00b64cade629acbfe1f5/Kourovka/Problems/P21_44/Solution.lean#L45), then follow density and shortening separately before the recurrence. Run `lake build Kourovka.Problems.P21_44.Solution` at the accepted revision; the [certificate guide](https://github.com/alunik/kourovka-lean/blob/5a6b2c18e326b7b0281f00b64cade629acbfe1f5/Kourovka/Problems/P21_44/Proof/Certificates/README.md) gives the data replay.

The [technical verification](../nilradical-v0-verification/README.md) records fresh project compilation, reviewed-statement comparison, and Lean plus Nanoda checking of six selected endpoints, permitting only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. The [independent statement audit](../nilradical-v0-verification/statement-audits/21.44.md) checks the exact natural action, full inverse limit, topology, and ordinary growth semantics. Human acceptance is recorded separately and does not certify this prose or novelty. Extracting a reusable entropy-counting criterion would be a reasonable further development; stronger quantitative bounds remain outside the accepted claim.
